en: The Ritual Manual for Making Offerings to the Seven Medicine-Buddhas, the Wish-Fulfilling King Sūtra;
Great Qing Imperially Commissioned Text on the West Heaven’s Great Benevolent Sovereign Buddha, Head of the Śākyan Teachings Throughout the World, Universal Wisdom Vajra-Holder, the Dalai Lama.
Composed by the Dalai Lama.
I prostrate to the Lord who is like a stainless full moon, Who benefits all sentient beings with the rain of Dharma.
Through the practice of the ritual procedures and the methods of aspiration, May all sufferings be extinguished and peace be attained.
These four lines of verse concern the origin of the aspiration for those who follow the path of faith.
The text is written in small characters arranged in parallel columns;
it is an old version translated by the ritual attendant Gongbu Chabu.
According to the Tibetan manuscript:
Extensively expounding the origins and lineages,
establishing the correct doctrine,
and arranging the ritual altar.
The sections on enshrining images,
making offerings, and so forth comprise more than thirty articles.
The text is extremely voluminous and largely consists of passages not intended for recitation;
there is no need to translate it in its entirety.
What follows is the ritual for the maṇḍala offering.
The following items are listed below.
Regarding the ritual for constructing the Bhaiṣajyaguru Maṇḍala,
there are those who may construct the maṇḍala-paṭa.
Alternatively, one may paint a maṇḍala;
any of these methods is acceptable.
Or again, one may enshrine Śākyamuni Buddha.
The images of the Seven Tathāgatas of Bhaiṣajyaguru,
as well as the various great Bodhisattvas, the Dharma-protectors, and the twelve yakṣas,
each according to their appropriate form.
Offerings of incense, lamps,
and flowers should be arranged according to the Dharma; these ritual items should be prepared and provided as the occasion requires.
One must strive for sincerity and purity.
Those who wish to practice this should bathe themselves until clean.
Put on new clothes.
For the purpose of the external bath,
one must abstain from impure foods such as meat, wine, garlic, and onions.
By consuming pure foods such as the three white and three sweet items,
one distances oneself from a defiled mind.
As for this internal bathing:
by means of this dharma-gate, those practitioners who are householders shall abide securely in the observance of the fast and precepts, while those who have left the home life shall likewise do so.
I observe the Mahāyāna fast and precepts;
as this is the most essential matter,
I look up with hope that the Three Jewels, in their absolute truth, and all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will grant their protection and guidance.
The supreme power of the perfection of the two accumulations;
the inconceivable supreme power of the purity of the dharmadhātu;
the gurus and all buddhas.
Together with his disciples,
he has descended to this field of merit at the place where the *poṣadha* is observed;
may he bestow the power of this sublime truth.
Descend and take your seat;
conceive this with resolute conviction.
Out of compassion for sentient beings in this age of the five turbidities, [I present] the Meaning of the Heart-Treasury of the Mahāvaipulya Sūtra.
I pay homage to the venerable masters who uphold my own lineage and tradition through their majestic power;
To the Bhagavān, who possesses great compassion, the guide endowed with omniscience,
Whose ocean of merit, wisdom, and excellence is profound— I pay homage to all the Tathāgatas.
Pure and far removed from the dust of desire, Skillfully liberated from all evil realms,
The single flavor, supreme, and most excellent truth— To that peaceful and wondrous Dharma I pay homage; Having understood it,
I shall proclaim it so that others may understand, And I shall dwell well within the various precepts of training.
Possessing all virtues, the supreme field of merit— I pay homage and prostrate to the Saṅgha.
I prostrate to the Most Honored One, the Perfectly Enlightened One; I prostrate to the Greatly Beneficent, the Right and Sublime Dharma;
I prostrate to the Vast Assembly of the Saṅgha. Forever I sincerely prostrate to the Triple Gem.

Clearly perceiving all sentient beings of the ten directions, Turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma throughout the ten directions, Rescuing and delivering all sentient beings of the ten directions— To all Buddhas of the ten directions, I pay homage.
With one mind, we together give rise to this rare vow: In the times and stages of practicing the Way, may we also be companions.
I pay homage to the thousand Buddhas who have brought to completion the events of this single Bhadrakalpa.
In the past, countless eons ago, you made various wondrous vows to rescue sentient beings from the depths of suffering and poverty. I pay homage to these eight Sugatas.
Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa,
and Śākyamuni, the God among Gods— To these seven valiant Buddhas I pay homage.
To you with the stainless moon-like face and sublime form, With a body of purple-gold, I pay homage.
Far removed from dust and defilement, beyond the three realms, Perfectly and equally awakened—I pay homage to the World-Honored One of Great Compassion who gathers all with impartiality.
Upon hearing his name, the sufferings of the evil realms are stilled;
He who removes the diseases of the three poisons, the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru, And the Buddha Lapis Lazuli Light—I pay homage to you.
To the place where a Perfectly Awakened One descends into birth, where he attains enlightenment,
where he turns the Great Wheel of Peaceful Quiescence, and to the place of the untainted cessation—
I pay homage to the Sugata who dwells eternally in every direction, and to the ground upon which he walks, strolls, sits, and stands.
I pay homage to all such places where [the Buddha] slept peacefully in the lion’s posture—
whether above, below, or in the center; in every direction and intermediate quarter,
wherever there may be a relic or no relic— I pay homage to all those precious stūpas.
The Perfection of Wisdom is ineffable, beyond thought, and beyond description; unborn and unceasing, it is like space.
I pay homage to that which arises as wisdom according to the nature of each class of beings.
I pay respectful homage to the Mother of the Buddhas of the three times, to Mañjuśrī, the Lord of Secrets who rescues and liberates, and to Avalokiteśvara and others of vast conduct.
I pay homage to the Saṅgha of the Mahāyāna, who delight in taking on the burden of delivering sentient beings and are at ease in both saṃsāra and nirvāṇa;
To those whose minds are the wondrous luminosity of the perfectly full precious light, and who manifest their bodies [for others], I prayfully pay homage;
To those who bestow peace and happiness even upon those who would cause them harm—in such places as these, I take refuge.
I pay homage to the sixteen Arhats, whose supreme wisdom is truly realized and whose faculties are fully disciplined;
who, in accordance with the Buddha’s teachings, remain in the world for a long time to propagate the Dharma and act as its protectors;
who have cultivated the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination and attained the fruit of the wisdom of the Pratyekabuddhas.
I pay homage to those who realize through self-awakening without relying on teachers, To the noble ones and pratyekabuddhas;

I pay homage to you. Possessing the great power of transformation and supernormal faculties, Having already accomplished your skillful wonders at the Buddha’s command, And being well able to guard the precious treasury of the Dharma— O Vajra Protector of the Teaching, I pay homage to you.
Through the vast accumulation of roots of merit from oceans of past generosity, you have attained the auspicious endowments of long life, wealth, grain, and resources,
providing nourishment and protection for those who practice the Way. To all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the entirety of space who continue these acts of giving wealth—
unto them we offer praise and prostrations, we and all sentient beings without exception.
I emanate bodies as numerous as the atoms of all lands,
To pay respectful homage at all times To all the Lions among Men throughout the worlds of the ten directions In the three periods of time;
With my pure body, speech, and mind, I prostrate everywhere until none remain.
By the majestic spiritual power of the Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna, I appear before all Tathāgatas;
From one body, I manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms of all lands, And pay homage to every Buddha throughout those lands, as many as their atoms.
Within each atom, there are Buddhas as numerous as its atoms, Each dwelling amidst the assemblies of Bodhisattvas.
So too are the atoms within the inexhaustible Dharma-realm;
With deep faith that all Buddhas pervade them entirely, Each, with oceans of every possible sound, Universally utters inexhaustible, wondrous words and phrases.
Throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, They praise the Buddhas' ocean of profound virtues.
Having completed the prostrations,
each returns to their original position.
The drums, trumpets, and various musical instruments [are played].
While performing the ritual actions and reciting:
With the most excellent and wondrous flower garlands, Music, scented unguents, and parasols—
With such supreme articles of adornment, I make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
With the most excellent garments and the most excellent incense, with powdered incense, burning incense,
and lamps and candles— each as vast as Mount Sumeru— I offer them all to all the Tathāgatas.
With a mind of vast and supreme resolve, I have deep faith in all the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Through the power of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, may I universally make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
[Pause. Then recite again:
All the evil karmas I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now repent for them all.
To all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, And to those of the Two Vehicles, both with and without further training,
I rejoice in all the merits of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
To all the Lamps of the World throughout the ten directions, Who first accomplished awakening,
I now entreat them all To turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma.
If any Buddhas manifest nirvana, I shall with utmost sincerity entreat them all:
"May you remain for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Whatever worship, praise, and offerings I make to the Buddhas, I request the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma.
Rejoicing in and repenting of all roots of goodness, and dedicating them toward sentient beings and the path of the Buddha—
having thus completed these seven branches,
place the right knee upon the ground.
With palms joined and sincere mindfulness, one receives the meaning of the *poṣadha*. How so?
One recollects: "In the past, there was the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
Like a well-trained king of horses or a great king of elephants,
he performs what ought to be done.
What was to be done has been accomplished;
the heavy burden has been laid down;
one's own benefit has been attained.
Having exhausted all fetters of existence,
possessing true speech and a well-liberated mind,
one is liberated through right knowledge.
They may think it is for the sake of convenience for sentient beings,
for the sake of their benefit,
for the sake of their liberation, or for the sake of their freedom from illness.
In order to prevent famine;
in order to perfect the methods for attaining enlightenment; and in order to increase and perfect the supreme, perfect awakening of unsurpassed bodhi.
I truly undertake the observance of the poṣadha precepts;
likewise, I, [name], shall also do so at this time.
When the sun rises at dawn, one should actually perform the *poṣadha* in this manner, reciting it three times.
Once the perception that the precepts have been received is established,
it is further advisable to memorize the specific items of those precepts.
Recite: From this day forth,
I shall not kill living beings, nor shall I take the wealth of others,
nor engage in sexual misconduct, nor speak words of falsehood.
Because they give rise to many faults, one should abstain from all intoxicants and not drink them;
one should not sit on high or broad beds; furthermore, one should renounce eating at improper times and refrain from wearing perfumes, garlands, or ornaments;
and one should not engage in singing, dancing, or music.
Just as the Honored One, the Worthy One of old, forever severed killing and other [evils], so may I, through such precepts, attain the unsurpassed fruit;
may I pull out those beings distressed by suffering from the ocean of misery. (Recite three times)

Oṃ amogha-haśire / sambara-sambara / bharabara / mahā-aśubhadaha / sadhapatama / bibukhi ita / bujadahara dahara / samanata / avārakita / hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is called the dhāraṇī of pure ethical discipline.
Recite seven times:
Firmly maintaining the prohibitive precepts, free from defilement, Fully endowed with purity, without transgression,
And detached from clinging to the precepts and so forth— May the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*) be fulfilled.
Having made such vows as above,
one then receives the Mahāyāna poṣadha dharma.
Having completed the reception of the precepts,
one should contemplate with thoughts of reverence and joy,
taking refuge as follows: "I take refuge, I take refuge in all Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three periods of time."
The virtuous activities of body, speech,
and mind fundamentally subsume the self-nature,
giving rise to the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma.
To the sovereign of all noble Saṅghas,
the kind Root Guru,
and the lineage gurus endowed with the majesty of the tradition.
I take refuge in the Buddha, I take refuge in the Dharma, I take refuge in the Saṅgha; I take refuge in the Buddha, I take refuge in the Dharma, I take refuge in the Saṅgha—recite the above as usual.
I take refuge in the World-Honored One, the Assembly of the Eight Great Sugatas of the Bhaisajyaguru Buddha.
Together with their retinues, [recite this] three times or seven times,
generating the bodhicitta for the sake of all sentient beings.
May I attain the fruit of Buddhahood.
For this purpose, I reverently practice the assembly of the Eight Great Tathāgatas of the World-Honored One.
Together with their retinues,
they pay homage, make offerings, and offer prayers for the sake of the supreme path of wondrous intent and so forth.
They abide in successive order.

From within the essence of *tathatā* (suchness), one gives rise to the four immeasurable minds; from within the essence of *tathatā*, one gives rise to the four immeasurable minds for myself and all sentient beings.
The nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is originally identical,
yet sentient beings have not yet awakened to this principle;
may all sentient beings be constantly endowed with peace and happiness.
And for the sake of establishing the causes of karma,
I pray that they may forever be free from suffering and its causes.
May they be free from all suffering and never depart from pure happiness;
may they completely relinquish attachment and aversion,
as well as the discrimination between the near and the distant.
One should dwell forever in a mind of equanimity regarding the causes of suffering and pleasure.
The Great Master of the Tiger’s Den said:
"Those who wish to practice [should do so as follows]."
First, one should exert all effort in self-observation;
once this merit of the *anātman* meditative concentration has arisen,
one thereby gives rise to the four immeasurable minds (*catur-apramāṇa*).
And as for the bodhicitta,
it is all for the sake of those sentient beings who are in ignorance; thus, these words analyze the sequence of cause and effect,
which is generally determined by the four immeasurable minds (*catur-apramāṇa*).
In brief, there are two types: the bodhicitta and the four immeasurable minds.
The fundamental intention is the same.
As for those who single-mindedly resolve to attain bodhicitta,
the explanation for this is found in the following text.
This elucidation of the ritual procedures accords with the meaning of the Great Master’s sūtras.
Among the four types of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), this concerns the empowerment of the sanctuary. I look up to the Three Jewels for their truthfulness.
May all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas grant their protection and empowerment.
Through the most supreme power of the perfection of the two accumulations and the inconceivable power of the purification of the dharmadhātu,
I pray that we shall reverently observe the ritual procedures as set forth in the *Saptabuddhaka-sūtra*, the Sutra on the Original Vows of the Seven Tathāgatas.
The assembly altar where the Tathāgatas of the ten directions,
together with their disciples and all the holy ones who protect the Dharma, have gathered.
Together with these various offerings, [I dedicate them] to those Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who,
through the power of their past vows, have manifested pure Buddha-lands,
as well as to Amitābha Buddha.
The world of Ultimate Bliss is fully endowed with all manner of meritorious adornments;
such is its ground.
All are composed of various kinds of precious jewels;
they are as level as the palm of a hand,
vast and boundless.
Stainless radiance shines forth, with subtle, pleasant, soft, and soothing touches;
various celestial flowers are scattered about, each possessing the fragrance of gośīrṣa sandalwood, and the walls are constructed of precious bricks.
Gold, silver, and pearls are scattered like sand over the ground;
there are utpala flowers.
The *kumuda* and lotuses spread and fill [the pond] in rapid succession.
The waters possess the eight virtues;
the ponds and pools are crystal clear,
exquisitely adorned with various kinds of aquatic birds.
Chanting harmonious and elegant sounds,
they joyfully soar and fly;
there are various kinds of wish-fulfilling jewel trees.
Each tree was fully adorned with divine maṇi jewels;
pearl necklaces hung down with suspended precious gems,
and flowers and fruits were in full bloom.
Resplendent and fully matured,
it was at that time slightly stirred by the breeze,
with golden bells suspended from it.
Trembling, it produces the sublime sound of the Dharma;
its rows are magnificently adorned,
and thus the ground of jewels is abundant and complete.
It is spontaneously accomplished.
Furthermore, the house and the maṇḍala-pavilion are consecrated; moreover, within the earth, they are composed of the seven precious jewels.
The immeasurable great hall radiates a great light that fills immeasurable worlds.
Exquisite and beautiful in manifold ways, with boundless excellence and infinite subtlety,
it transcends all realms of the three worlds and surpasses the mundane sphere.
By means of those unsurpassed roots of goodness, [it brings about this result].
It gives rise to pure accomplishment;
it is the sovereign, awakened, luminous essence and characteristic,
the dwelling place of the Tathāgata.
Together with the assembly of noble Bodhisattvas,
and the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and garuḍas.
Kinnaras, mahoragas,
humans, non-humans, and others sport within it in countless numbers.
Sustaining oneself with the flavor of the Dharma,
may one be ever joyful and vow to deliver all sentient beings.
May they forever obtain benefit;
may they remain far removed from all afflictions, enmities, harms, stains, and obstacles;
and may they forever abandon all demonic activities.
Adorned with all manner of splendors throughout the world,
it is beyond compare,
resembling the pure land of a Buddha.
The great wisdom of mental intention:
thorough awakening and certainty in the śamatha and vipaśyanā of one's own vehicle.
He enters the gateways of liberation:
emptiness, signlessness,
and wishlessness— the king of precious lotuses.
Immeasurable merits serve as the adornments for these immeasurable jewel palaces,
which are spontaneously accomplished.
Next, regarding the consecration of the seat within the precious mandala:
upon a lotus lion throne of jewels is the Tathāgata Śrīkīrtivimalatejorāja.
The Tathāgata Ratnacandrapadmaprajñavyūhaghoṣarāja;
the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇavimalaratnaprabhasucaritasamudgata;
the Tathāgata Aśoka-vara-śrī.
The Tathāgata Dharma-Ocean Thunder-Sound;
the Tathāgata Supreme Wisdom of the Dharma-Ocean Sporting in Supernormal Powers;
and the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaidūryaprabha-rāja.
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni,
the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,
and all the holy deities.
The assembly for protecting the Dharma shall arrange their seats according to the respective holy ones.
Elicited by the power of vows,
it is radiant, abundant,
and spontaneously accomplished.
Furthermore, regarding the consecrated offerings:

in all internal and external locations, one should provide various most excellent offerings for the enjoyment of devas and humans, such as food and drink, clothing, music, and other extraordinary varieties of ritual requisites, each according to its appropriate kind.
Just as recorded in the Tripiṭaka Sūtras and the Bhadracarīpraṇidhāna Sūtra,
all offering articles are like clouds and like oceans.
Pure, abundant, and overflowing,
with all adornments arrayed;
may all the noble ones [be present].
May this assembly receive secret empowerment.
I also pray that you will compassionately accept [this offering], three times.
"The Universal Sage’s Cloud of Offerings, Vast and Greatly Joyful."
Recite the *Dhāraṇī of the Cloud of Offerings*,
as stated in the *Sūtra of Increasing Great Benefit*: *Om namaḥ bhagavate*.
Balarasa alabalamala dandata taga da ayā.
